title_ar: فضيلة العلامة محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يحاضر عن شمائل النبي (ص)
title_en: His Eminence the Erudite Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, Head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures on the Traits of the Prophet
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة في دار الشباب القديمة بانواكشوط مساء أمس الخميس، تحت عنوان: "هو الرحمة المهداة". تطرق الشيخ – حفظه الله- في هذه المحاضرة لأمور مهمة نجملها في ما يلي: • - كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم رحمة مهداة يدل على عناية الله تعالى بهذه الأمة. • - تشريف الله تعالى لهذه الأمة أن أرسل إليها أعظم البشرية وهو خاتم النبيئين، وأنزل عليه القرآن هدى للناس وبينات؛ معجز في ألفاظه ومعانيه. • - من رحمته المهداة أن جعل في أمته من يقوم بشأن النبوة ويجدد لها دينها، وهم العلماء ورثة الأنبياء. • - من رحمته المهداة ما أخبر عنه (ص) من مراتب السياسة والخير والشر التي تمر بها أمته، وهو ما أشار له الحديث الشريف: "تَكُونُ النُّبُوَّةُ فِيكُمْ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَكُونَ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُهَا إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ خِلاَفَةٌ عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ النُّبُوَّةِ فَتَكُونُ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَكُونَ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُهَا إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكاً عَاضًّا فَيَكُونُ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُهَا إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكاً جَبْرِيَّةً فَيَكُونُ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُهَا إِذَا شَاءَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ خِلاَفَةٌ عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ نُبُوَّةٍ ثُمَّ سَكَتَ". • - من رحمته المهداة أيضا كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم قرآنا يمشي على وجه الأرض، كما في حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها " كان خلقه القرآن". • - من رحمته المهداة أن جعل القرآن العظيم المنزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، رحمة في قراءته وأحكامه وشفاعته يوم القيامة فهو الرحمة الخالدة في الأرض، الناطق بالحق والحجة البالغة على الناس أجمعين • - تتجلى هذه الرحمة في وسطية التشريع والليونة في الأحكام والتكاليف، وهي ميزة الإسلام عن غيره من الملل والنحل. هذه أبرز الأفكار التي تناولتها هذه المحاضرة. ونشير هنا إلى أن هذه المحاضرة تم تنظيمها من طرف جمعية الفتاة للتوعية ومكافحة التسرب المدرسي، وحضرها جمهور غفير من رواد الجمعية ومحبي الشيخ، كما حضرها ممثلون من بعض الجمعيات الأخرى.
body_en:
His eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture at the old Youth House in Nouakchott yesterday evening, Thursday, under the title: "He is the Mercy Bestowed". The Sheikh — may God preserve him — dealt in this lecture with important matters, which we summarise as follows:

• That he — may God bless him and grant him peace — is a mercy bestowed indicates God Most High's care for this community.

• God Most High's honouring of this community, in that He sent to it the greatest of humankind, the Seal of the Prophets, and sent down upon him the Qur'an as guidance for people and as clear proofs, inimitable in its wording and in its meanings.

• Part of his being a mercy bestowed is that He placed within his community those who uphold the business of prophethood and renew its religion for it — and they are the scholars, the heirs of the prophets.

• Part of his being a mercy bestowed is what he — may God bless him and grant him peace — foretold of the stages of governance, and of the good and the evil, through which his community would pass; which is what the noble report points to: "Prophethood will be among you for as long as God wills it to be, then He will raise it up when He wills to raise it up. Then there will be a caliphate on the pattern of prophethood, and it will be for as long as God wills it to be, then He will raise it up when He wills to raise it up. Then there will be a biting kingship, and it will be for as long as God wills it to be, then He will raise it up when He wills to raise it up. Then there will be a coercive kingship, and it will be for as long as God wills it to be, then He will raise it up when He wills to raise it up. Then there will be a caliphate on the pattern of prophethood." Then he fell silent.

• Part of his being a mercy bestowed also is that he — may God bless him and grant him peace — was a Qur'an walking upon the face of the earth, as in the report of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: "his character was the Qur'an".

• Part of his being a mercy bestowed is that He made the mighty Qur'an, sent down upon Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — a mercy in its recitation, in its rulings and in its intercession on the Day of Resurrection; for it is the abiding mercy upon the earth, that which speaks the truth, and the conclusive proof against all people.

• This mercy is made manifest in the balance of the legislation and in the flexibility of the rulings and the obligations, and this is what distinguishes Islam from the other creeds and sects.

These are the most prominent ideas that this lecture dealt with. We note here that this lecture was organised by the Girl's Association for Awareness and Combating School Drop-out, and was attended by a large audience of the association's regulars and of those who love the Sheikh, as well as by representatives of some other associations.

flags.arabic: ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكاً عَاضًّا ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ مُلْكاً جَبْرِيَّةً ... ثُمَّ تَكُونُ خِلاَفَةٌ عَلَى مِنْهَاجِ نُبُوَّةٍ
flags.context: the long report on the stages of governance, quoted in the summary of the lecture
options: render the stages literally — biting kingship, coercive kingship — and add no attribution or grading
render them interpretively as hereditary and tyrannical rule
add the collection and grading of the report
flags.note: Editorially sensitive, and sensitive to its date. This report is quoted in Nouakchott in February 2011, at the height of the Arab uprisings, in a lecture summary that presents it as a prophecy of the stages of rule his community would pass through, ending in a restored caliphate. It is read politically by all sides. The stage names are rendered literally rather than interpretively, so that the English does not put a contemporary application into the Sheikh's mouth that the summary does not contain. The source gives no narrator, collection or grading, and style guide section 4 forbids adding one; none has been added. Everything here is the site editor's summary of a spoken lecture, not the Sheikh's written words.

flags.context: the framing of the summarised points
options: keep the reporting frame visible and never present the points as the Sheikh's own words
present the points as direct statements by the Sheikh
flags.note: The site editor states that the points are his own summary of a spoken lecture, not a transcript. Every proposition is therefore second-hand and must not be quoted as the Sheikh's written words.

flags.context: the description of the Prophet in the second point
options: read as 'النبيين' (the prophets), the standard Qur'anic form
flags.note: 'النبيئين' is written with a hamza where the standard Qur'anic form at al-Aḥzāb 33:40 is 'النبيين'. The form with hamza is a recognised variant and not necessarily an error, but it is left exactly as served in body_ar and recorded rather than normalised.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh; the reporting frame is preserved throughout.

'الرحمة المهداة' is the lecture's title and echoes a well-known description of the Prophet; rendered 'the Mercy Bestowed' and kept consistent through the item, since the whole summary is built on repeating the phrase.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system. It is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en; the recording itself is out of scope for text translation.
